source: Diocesan Cycle of Prayer, Advent 2025 - Pentecost Season 2026
notes: Source covers Advent 2025 (November 30, 2025) through the Last Sunday after Pentecost/Christ the King (November 22, 2026) -- the November 30, 2025 entry is the only one before calendar year 2026 and is included since the source's own declared range begins there, matching this corpus's existing precedent for a cycle whose own stated scope spans a year boundary.

Every dated entry carries the source's own liturgical Sunday name (e.g. 'First Sunday of Advent', 'Palm Sunday') -- recorded in `liturgicalNote`, a disclosed label from the source, not computed by this app.

A real source anomaly, disclosed rather than silently merged or corrected: between 'Sunday, April 12, 2026' and 'Sunday, April 19, 2026' the source ALSO prints two entries dated 'Sunday, April 20, 2025' and 'Sunday, April 27, 2025' (year 2025, not 2026) with the identical liturgical labels 'Easter Day' and 'Second Sunday of Easter' and overlapping-but-not-identical subjects (Church of the Resurrection, Pleasant Hill + St. Anselm's, Lafayette; and St. Mark's, Berkeley/Palo Alto/Crockett). April 20, 2025 was independently confirmed a real Easter Sunday, and the entries are internally self-consistent for THAT year -- these are evidently leftover 2025-cycle entries from an earlier version of this document that were not fully removed when it was updated for 2025-26, not typos of 2026 dates (the document's own 2026 Easter season, April 5/12/19/26, is already separately and completely present). Excluded from `entries` here since they fall entirely outside this file's own declared 'Advent 2025 - Pentecost Season 2026' range (April 2025 predates Advent 2025) -- not fabricated content, not a gap in this transcription.

A footnote in the source discloses two commemoration sources for April 12, 2026's own subjects, quoted here rather than attached piecemeal to that entry: 'The commemoration of Rev. Daniel Gee Ching Wu can be found in "Great Cloud of Witnesses" -- an alternative book of remembrances on the Episcopal Calendar. The commemoration of Rev. Peter Williams Cassey and Annie Besant Cassey can be found in "Lesser Feasts and Fasts" -- a publication of the Episcopal Church.'
